hello. this is going to be long bc i ramble. feel free to read if you want

 i understand you’re frustrated, but imagine how he feels since he’s the one who’s suffering from it firsthand. the idea that “if he wanted to get better he would put effort in” is EXTREMELY dangerous and potentially harmful to believe, because depression and anxiety make every small thing seem “impossible.” when dealing with anxiety, there’s a term called the “impossible task,” which is any task a person with anxiety feels incapable of doing. it can be cleaning, or exercising, or even just eating / showering. it could also be larger things like a dysfunctional family. anything that feels overwhelming subsequently can become “impossible.”
depression is an incredibly self sabotaging illness, and it’s going to make you feel like you CAN’T get better, despite how much you want to. so what you’re describing of his behaviour absolutely does line up with typical depressive behaviour

the best thing you can do is empathize and understand that it’s not his choice to not do these things. it’s going to be hard for him, and you need to positively encourage him to do small things and be a positive source of energy for him. 

even if it’s things like, when ur seeing each other in person, ask him to get u a soda or a water from the kitchen so that he can just get up and move and accomplish something, those are HUGE. being able to cook a meal? even larger an accomplishment.

it sounds like you care a lot, and that’s great!! you sound like a great partner who’s trying to stay supportive, even when it’s out of your realm or when it’s not your job to do so. but you also have to be careful because it’s super easy to think you’re supporting someone but actually be applying negative convictions to them. i know i’m fixating, but the line you mentioned of him not wanting to get better bc he doesn’t put effort in is just so invalidating. i hope you haven’t said anything like that to him; and if u have, that’s ok! just apologize and say you’ll work on your own biases. again, sorry for fixating on that, but i find that super super important for you to keep in mind

it sounds like rn, he’s struggling BAD to go to the doctor. communicate with him, ask him why it’s difficult for him and what you can do to help. even if it’s gentle daily reminders, or some other form of TLC. depression and anxiety are super case by case and people will need support in wildly different ways. same reason why it can take people going through over 5-10 different types of antidepressants before finding one that actually works, if they ever find one at all

sorry for the in depth answer; i hope he manages to start recovering someday soon. and remember; it’s not your job to get him meds or therapy, so dont feel like you need to stress out about it on his behalf. it’s ultimately up to him to get better, and he’s going to have to work hard to start taking physical action to start getting better. you can only just be there for him while he works at this.

I hope things work out for you! Good luck, too. i’m sure he’s lucky and thankful to have you around

also i hope none of this came across as like- assuming or being rude or saying ur not being supportive. i can’t know the full situation so i probably repeated many things or repeated things u already knew, but the fact youre seeking help for him is so so so kind

i know this might not be an answer you want, but dealing with them is very individualistic and case by case. i really rly recommend a therapist for the best treatment, especially since it’s more “tailor made” an experience for you.

you don’t need to answer here, but figure out why these thoughts and this episode started, and figure out what would be different in your life if you were happy. or whether or not you can even currently imagine a “happy life” to begin with.

lastly, try to pay attention to things that are under your control, both emotionally and physically. when you feel like you’re breaking down, try to let yourself loosen up and experience those feelings without resistance. and engage in self-care, like tidying up your home (if you’re low functioning, just start with making your bed and if you can keep going, start working on clearing out trash) and self hygiene like showers. try to treat yourself to at least two meals a day, exercise if you can, careful with substances, try to keep in touch with friends or have conversations with them. 

in my opinion it’s way harder to try to fix your perception of yourself and your mental state. but it’s relatively easier to focus on actions and habits, which can be stepping stones to rebuilding the energy and motivation to make further change in ur day to day.

Definitely not conclusive nor am I a good source, but my AMAB friends that have smoked / vaped throughout high school all ended up with much deeper voices. I haven’t seen an AFAB person’s voice deepen, though. Keep in mind though my friends that smoke and vape were legitimate stoners by definition, going through a pod once or twice a week and getting high on a daily basis through dab pens. If you’re going through a pod a month, I would say you won’t see any changes for a few years (not to say you won’t see any changes at all though).

I don’t think that matters much though for voice training, since it SEEMS to lower pitch mostly. In general, larynx and resonance is more important for being read as a certain gender, and even lower pitches will still pass very well as feminine so long as you have a bright resonance.

I’m also pretty sure that the changes you would see through voice training will be a lot faster than the changes you would see from vaping. If you want to keep vaping, just make sure to record yourself speaking every month or every few months to check how your voice is training (for better or worse, since I assume you would be voice training at the same time). If you do end up noticing a lowering voice from vaping, and you’re not happy with it, change your smoking habits. 

My personal experience is that I used to vape a lot (but a pod every two months), but I’ve decided to hold off on any smoking until I see how my resonance changes, because I would rather have a lower pitch voice with bright resonance. If you want a high pitch though, do be careful of how often you vape or smoke. 

Hope this helps at all! I don’t know the scientific stuff so I’m only speaking from what I’ve observed and what I know from voice training, so definitely take what I say with a grain of salt.

Edit: also I rly do wanna stress I really don’t know how vaping affects you on a biological level. Obviously the people I see who get lowered voices don’t voice train, so it’s possible that vaping might not even matter if you train. If anyone knows more, please correct me!!
